newsitem.title: USA: Octel slumps on Q1, product upgrade delay. [CORRECTED 19:32 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Octel slumps on Q1, product upgrade delay. [CORRECTED 19:32 GMT]

text.p: Octel Communications Corp shares fell 35 percent after the provider of voice processing systems reported first-quarter results below analysts' consensus estimate and told analysts that release of a product upgrade would be delayed.

"Management commented that there would be a three- to six-month delay in the release of a software upgrade for its Sierra platform," Merrill Lynch analyst Joseph Bellace said in a report. "We estimate that the delay...will reduce revenue by about $20 million in fiscal 1997."
Bellace cut his fiscal 1997 earnings estimate for Octel to a range of $1.00-1.20 a share, from $1.20-1.30.
He downgraded the stock to near-term neutral from accumulate and to long-term accumulate from buy.
Late Thursday Octel reported operating earnings for the quarter ended September 30 rose to $0.19 a share from $0.12 a year ago. Merrill said the consensus was $0.20.
Octel shares slumped 8-1/2 to 16 in Friday morning trading.
A spokesman for Octel said the company's quarterly earnings met the First Call consensus of $0.19 a share.
